findings.description: S3 bucket 'example-malformed-bucket' gives anyone on the internet CAN_READ (actions: s3:getobject); not verified: s3:account-public-access-block-unknown.
findings.remediation: Remove the wildcard Principal or scope it with a principal-restricting condition (aws:PrincipalOrgID, aws:SourceVpce, aws:SourceArn); keep Block Public Access (RestrictPublicBuckets) on at account level.
findings.title: Bucket 'example-malformed-bucket' is public through its bucket policy (CAN_READ)

findings.description: The Kubernetes API endpoint of cluster demo-unreachable (eu-west-2) is publicly accessible from 0.0.0.0/0. Authentication is still required, but any leaked kubeconfig, token or mapped IAM credential is usable from anywhere, and API-server vulnerabilities are exposed.
findings.remediation: Disable public endpoint access, or restrict publicAccessCidrs to known administration networks.
findings.title: EKS cluster demo-unreachable has a public API endpoint open to the internet

findings.description: No password policy is set: console passwords only need the AWS defaults (0 user(s) with a console password).
findings.remediation: Set an account password policy: length >= 14, all character classes, reuse prevention 24.
findings.title: The account has no IAM password policy

findings.description: The Kubernetes API was not enumerated for this cluster (no k8s data in the report) (cluster demo-err, eu-west-2). Pods, service accounts, RBAC and network objects of this cluster are unknown: the absence of Kubernetes edges and findings for it is not evidence of a safe cluster.
findings.remediation: Give the collecting identity read access to the cluster (an access entry or aws-auth mapping with the read-only RBAC of 'aws-enumerator permissions --k8s'), or use --k8s-auth kubeconfig/token, and re-run.
findings.title: Kubernetes objects of cluster demo-err were not enumerated
